items.q: Best prophylaxis backbone for highly emetogenic cisplatin chemotherapy combines which three?
o: 5HT3 blocker plus NK1 blocker plus dexamethasone
items.exp: Modern triplet prophylaxis blocks serotonin acutely, substance P for delayed phase and adds dexamethasone synergy, transforming cisplatin tolerability. Vestibular drugs do not address chemotherapy circuits.
r: Incorrect. Those target motion and dopamine pathways mainly.
Correct. Serotonin plus substance P plus steroid.
Incorrect. Single dopamine blockade fails cisplatin.
Incorrect. Histamine pathways are vestibular, not chemotherapeutic.
items.kp: Cisplatin prophylaxis: 5HT3 plus NK1 plus dexamethasone.

items.q: Ondansetron is notably ineffective for which vomiting type?
items.exp: Motion sickness travels vestibular histamine and muscarinic routes untouched by serotonin blockade, needing hyoscine or sedating antihistamines instead.
r: Incorrect. Postoperative vomiting responds well to 5HT3 blockade.
Incorrect. Chemotherapy vomiting is its flagship use.
Correct. Motion sickness ignores ondansetron.
Incorrect. Radiotherapy emesis also involves serotonin pathways.
items.kp: Car sick patient needs hyoscine, not ondansetron.

items.q: A young woman develops torticollis and oculogyric crisis hours after metoclopramide. This acute reaction is what?
o: Acute dystonia from central dopamine blockade
items.exp: Central D2 blockade in the young provokes acute dystonic reactions treated by stopping the drug and giving anticholinergics such as procyclidine. Tardive dyskinesia is the late hyperkinetic complication of chronic use.
r: Incorrect. Tardive appears after months, choreiform not dystonic spasm.
Correct. Acute dystonia follows early dopamine blockade.
Incorrect. Serotonin syndrome adds clonus, fever and agitation.
Incorrect. NMS evolves over days with rigidity and fever.
items.kp: Young, twisted neck after metoclopramide: acute dystonia.

items.q: Domperidone is restricted in dose and duration mainly because of which cardiac risk?
o: QT prolongation and sudden cardiac death
items.exp: Domperidone prolongs QT, especially in older patients, higher doses and interacting drugs, prompting regulatory limits despite its advantage of minimal brain penetration.
r: Incorrect. Its danger is repolarisation, not block.
Correct. QT prolongation drives the restrictions.
Incorrect. Pressure crisis is not its signature harm.
Incorrect. It treats no arrhythmia.
items.kp: Domperidone spares brain but taxes the QT interval.

items.q: Delayed vomiting two to five days after chemotherapy is best prevented by blocking which receptor?
items.exp: Substance P acting at NK1 receptors drives the delayed phase that serotonin blockade misses, so aprepitant added to prophylaxis specifically covers days two to five.
r: Incorrect. H1 drugs serve vestibular vomiting.
Correct. NK1 blockade owns the delayed phase.
Incorrect. Muscarinic drugs serve motion sickness.
Incorrect. Dopamine alone cannot cover delayed emesis.
items.kp: Late chemotherapy vomiting equals substance P; block NK1.

items.q: Hyoscine patches prevent motion sickness by blocking which receptors in vestibular pathways?
items.exp: Scopolamine (hyoscine) antimuscarinic action dampens vestibular to vomiting centre signalling, with dry mouth, blurred vision and confusion as expected anticholinergic costs, especially in elderly travellers.
r: Incorrect. Serotonin blockade fails motion sickness.
Correct. Muscarinic blockade calms vestibular input.
Incorrect. NK1 belongs to chemotherapy delayed phase.
Incorrect. H2 blockade reduces stomach acid only.
items.kp: Motion sickness patch equals anticholinergic hyoscine.

items.q: Metoclopramide helps diabetic gastroparesis through which dual action?
o: Dopamine blockade antiemesis plus upper gut prokinesis
items.exp: Metoclopramide blocks dopamine inhibition of gut motility and adds cholinergic facilitation, emptying the stomach while its central D2 blockade stops nausea, a pairing unique among antiemetics.
r: Incorrect. That describes ulcer therapy, not motility.
Correct. Antiemetic plus prokinetic in one drug.
Incorrect. Laxatives act on colon, not gastric stasis.
Incorrect. Enzymes aid pancreatic insufficiency digestion.
items.kp: Gastroparesis drug must move the stomach, not just mask nausea.

items.q: Anticipatory vomiting in chemotherapy patients is best managed primarily how?
o: Optimal prophylaxis from cycle one plus behavioural therapy and short anxiolytic
items.exp: Conditioned vomiting learns from badly controlled early cycles, so flawless initial prophylaxis, desensitisation and lorazepam type anxiolysis outperform escalating receptor blockers for a cortical reflex.
r: Incorrect. Receptor escalation cannot unlearn conditioning.
Correct. Prevention plus behavioural care leads.
Incorrect. Vestibular patches miss the cortical circuit.
Incorrect. Abandoning curative therapy is disproportionate.
items.kp: Prevent vomiting perfectly in cycle one or the brain learns it.

items.q: Which antiemetic adjunct also treats migraine nausea and is given with triptans?
items.exp: Metoclopramide's prokinetic action reverses migraine gastric stasis improving triptan absorption while its dopamine blockade relieves nausea, making it the migraine antiemetic of choice.
r: Incorrect. Aprepitant is chemotherapy prophylaxis.
Correct. Metoclopramide partners triptans in migraine.
Incorrect. Hyoscine targets motion sickness.
Incorrect. Cyclizine lacks the prokinetic migraine benefit.
items.kp: Migraine stomach stalls: metoclopramide moves it.

items.q: In hyperemesis gravidarum, which supportive step must accompany antiemetics to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy?
o: Thiamine replacement with fluids and electrolytes
items.exp: Prolonged vomiting depletes thiamine; glucose containing fluids without thiamine can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy, so thiamine precedes or accompanies rehydration in hyperemesis care.
r: Incorrect. Vitamin K addresses coagulopathy, not this brain risk.
Correct. Thiamine protects the vomiting brain.
Incorrect. Iron treats anaemia, unrelated to encephalopathy.
Incorrect. Folate prevents neural tube defects, not Wernicke.
items.kp: Vomiting plus glucose without thiamine risks Wernicke.
